events.credibility_reason: Sampling estimate with author-only error bars; figures known only from search excerpts; symmetry step appears to be the identity term of Burnside only.
Restated sampling estimate; excerpted per-grid mean does not reproduce the excerpted totals; text not read.
Non-academic restatement that mislabels the Berthier minimal-puzzle estimate as a count of unique-solution puzzles.

why: The statement asks for the number of minimal puzzles; nothing in the record determines or rigorously bounds it after January 2024. The Berthier figures are statistical estimates, not proven bounds, so they score none rather than bound. Royle's 49,151 17-clue list is an explicit lower bound on the count (every 17-clue unique puzzle is minimal), so bound, but it predates the snapshot. McGuire et al. settle the minimum clue count, a fact about minimal puzzles' sizes rather than their number: none. Tjusila et al. and Eppstein–Zhang answer per-grid minimum-clue questions and An et al. count minimal games on 5×5 perfect-code grids: all changed questions, so variant. Pereira counts grids, and the blog restates old figures: none. No AI system appears in any event.
doubts: The statement names no grid size or symmetry convention; I read it as standard 9×9 per its Sudoku parent. Treating Royle's list as a bound on the total is generous but immaterial since it predates the snapshot.
